title: Anatomo-clinico-biological Profiles in Severe Nasal Polyps
official: Anatomo-clinico-biological Profiles in Severe Nasal Polyps
summary:
Nasal sinus polyposis is a chronic inflammatory pathology of the nasal cavity and sinus cavities that causes bilateral and multifocal polyp development and has a prevalence of 2 to 4% in the general population.

Therapeutic management consists of first-line medical treatment for anti-inflammatory purposes. Local corticosteroid therapy, using nasal sprays, is the background treatment. Surgical management is offered to patients in case of failure of medical treatment. Although effective, surgery does not protect patients from recurrence of symptoms related to regrowth of polyps. Recently, biologics have appeared, which despite its effectiveness, about 20% of patients have a partial or no response to these treatments. There is currently no possibility of determining the probability of response to treatments in patients.

It is therefore essential to determine an anatomo-clinico-biological correlation associating the anatomopathological profile, the clinical characteristics and the cytokine signature in order to best guide the patient's management, including the initiation of biotherapy. Indeed, patients, according to their clinical, biological characteristics and the cytokine signature of their polyps will react differently to different treatments, including surgery and biotherapy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients ≥ 18 years old.
* Patients diagnosed with a CRSwNP resistant to medical treatment, who are scheduled to undergo a first-time endoscopic sinus surgery (with ethmoidectomy).
* Free subjects, without guardianship or curatorship or subordination.
* Patients having signed the consent form.
* Patients benefitting from a Social Security system.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Current or past biotherapy treatment.
* Use of systemic corticosteroids within 4 weeks prior to surgery.
* Persons requiring enhanced protection, namely minors, individuals deprived of their liberty by a judicial or administrative decision, individuals residing in a health or social care facility, adults under legal guardianship.
* Pregnant women or lactating women.
